title: Answer: no account of what information is, which the theory sorts by how accessible it is

statements.text: The global workspace theory takes no position on what information is. It takes information as what the nervous system encodes and sorts it by access to the workspace: some is permanently inaccessible, some is in contact with the workspace and could become conscious if attended to, and at any moment only a subset of the latter is mobilized into the workspace and is conscious.
statements.scope: the 2001 workspace framework of Dehaene and Naccache, section 6.2

sources.quote: Some information encoded in the nervous system is permanently inaccessible (set I1).
However, at any given time, only a subset of the latter is mobilized into the workspace (set I3).
